reversals.claim: I've switched my major focus from history to economics.
reversals.user_update_task: I've switched my major focus from history to economics, so can you help me write a short email introducing myself to my new advisor?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Semester plan. Officially declared economics as my major focus last week, history is now just a minor. Courses: Intermediate Microeconomics, Econometrics I, Money and Banking, and one history seminar to finish the minor. Need to brush up on calculus before econometrics starts and get R installed on my laptop. Met with the economics advisor on Tuesday, next meeting in October. Withdrew my application for the history honors track. Goal: find a research assistant position in the economics department by spring.

reversals.claim: I've gone back to handwritten notes and abandoned Obsidian.
reversals.user_update_task: I've gone back to handwritten notes and abandoned Obsidian, can you suggest a good way to index my paper notebooks?
reversals.own_notes_doc: New study setup, started this term. Deleted the Obsidian vault from my laptop after exporting it as a backup. Bought three A5 dot-grid notebooks, one per course, and a set of fineliners. I write everything by hand in lectures and in the library now, and I remember it much better. Using colored tabs to mark sections and a page-numbered contents list at the front of each notebook. The laptop stays in my bag during lectures. Need to find a way to carry fewer notebooks on long days.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here are my notes about my study setup. Can you suggest small improvements to it?
reversals.probe: What's a good way to organize my notes for the new term?

reversals.claim: I've started studying alone; the group wasn't working for me.
reversals.user_update_task: I've started studying alone since the group wasn't working for me, so can you help me plan focused study blocks for this week?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Oct 2: Told the study group I'm leaving. Sessions kept drifting into chatting and I wasn't getting through the reading. Oct 3: First solo session on the quiet floor of the library, three hours, finished two chapters. Oct 5: Solo again, wrote the essay outline. Oct 8: Got much more done this week than in any week with the group. Oct 10: Might still ask one classmate to swap essay drafts once a month, but daily study stays solo from now on. Need a better routine for evenings.
reversals.own_notes_task: Can you read my October study log and tell me what's working and what I should keep doing?
reversals.probe: Can you help me plan my study schedule for this week?

reversals.claim: I've shifted from early-modern to contemporary history.
reversals.user_update_task: I've shifted from early-modern to contemporary history, so can you suggest some archives I should look into for my thesis?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Thesis topic change approved today. Moving from early-modern trade to contemporary history: the topic is now European migration policy from 1990 to 2015. New supervisor is in the modern history group. Need to drop the paleography course and take the oral history methods seminar instead. Sources will be parliamentary records, newspapers, and interviews. Returned the seventeenth-century source books to the library. Next: draft a new research question and submit the ethics application for the interviews by the end of the month.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here are my thesis notes. Can you help me turn them into a timeline for the next two months?

reversals.claim: I've started relying on lecture recordings instead of reading.
reversals.user_update_task: I've started relying on lecture recordings instead of reading, so can you help me figure out how to take notes efficiently while watching them?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Study habits this term. I stopped doing the weekly readings and now rely on the lecture recordings instead. I watch each lecture at 1.5x speed on the evening it's posted and pause to write down key points. The professors cover the main arguments anyway, and I get through the material in half the time. Seminar prep is now rewatching the relevant part of the lecture. Next: build a playlist of recordings for each exam topic so revision is easier, and check which seminars expect quotes from the texts.
